# Option A: sectors, attenuators and ports (generated by option_a_sectors.py)

> The physical bench is now IF-conducted and is specified by bench_spec.py and blueprint.py (out/poc1_blueprint.pdf, out/poc1_cable_schedule.md); where they differ, they win. There, devices that die at t0 lose power at switched PDU outlets and take their paths down with them. PoC 1 has no programmable attenuators: each IF tile path carries a fixed pad stack sized from the values below (hub paths 'before', bridges 'after'; pad schedule, out/poc1_blueprint.pdf sheet 6), the bridges are held down with Terragraph ignition disabled until MARL engages them, and each IP-50 hop is a fixed 70 dB pad chain. The dB values below come from the V-band radio model with 20 dB pads and are placeholders until each path is calibrated on the real radios.

A - 8 IP-50 + 8 TG.

No steering emulation: the TG radios point their own beams, so only the final plan is cabled (the pre-event TG links plus the bridges E2–W2, E1–N, W1–S). Programmable attenuators set each path's loss and hold each bridge off-beam until its sites engage; on the bench, CORE and HUB are powered off at t0, which takes their paths down.

## Sectors per node

| Node | Type | Unit (sectors it faces) | Sectors used | Before the event | Final (after recovery) | Polarity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HUB | DN | 4-sector (E, N, W, S) | 3 (E, W, S) | E → E1, E2; W → W1, W2; S → S | off (destroyed) | E odd, W even, S odd |
| CORE | DN | 4-sector (E, N, W, S) | 1 (N) | N → N | off (destroyed) | N even |
| W1 | DN | 4-sector (E, N, W, S) | 2 (E, S) | E → HUB | S → S | E odd, S odd |
| W2 | DN | 4-sector (E, N, W, S) | 1 (E) | E → HUB | E → E2 | E odd |
| E1 | DN | 4-sector (E, N, W, S) | 2 (N, W) | W → HUB | N → N | N even, W even |
| E2 | DN | 4-sector (E, N, W, S) | 1 (W) | W → HUB | W → W2 | W even |
| S | CN | terminal | 1 (single) | single → HUB | single → W1 | single even |
| N | CN | terminal | 1 (single) | single → CORE | single → E1 | single odd |

Sectors in use: 10 on the 6 nodes (of 24 available) and 2 on the 2 terminals: 12 in all. 14 node sectors carry no link in the drawn plan; on the smaller units they are the spares that keep alternative bridges reachable (terminate their ports if they are RF-port builds).

Mounted this way, the units can reach 12 of the 12 feasible bridge candidates and 8 of the 8 valid recovery plans (MARL's choice of peer); each smaller unit's spare sector is chosen to keep as many as possible.

## V-band paths and programmable attenuators (dB)

| # | Path | Sector ports | Distance | Job | Before | At t0 | After | Margin up / at max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HUB–W1 | HUB-W ↔ W1-E | 324 m | taken down at t0 (island) | 27.6 | 63.0 | 63.0 | 21.6 / -13.9 |
| 2 | HUB–W2 | HUB-W ↔ W2-E | 324 m | taken down at t0 (island) | 23.1 | 63.0 | 63.0 | 21.6 / -18.4 |
| 3 | HUB–E1 | HUB-E ↔ E1-W | 324 m | taken down at t0 (island) | 27.6 | 63.0 | 63.0 | 21.6 / -13.9 |
| 4 | HUB–E2 | HUB-E ↔ E2-W | 324 m | taken down at t0 (island) | 23.1 | 63.0 | 63.0 | 21.6 / -18.4 |
| 5 | HUB–S | HUB-S ↔ S-single | 516 m | taken down at t0 (island) | 34.5 | 63.0 | 63.0 | 14.6 / -13.9 |
| 6 | CORE–N | CORE-N ↔ N-single | 270 m | taken down at t0 (island) | 25.2 | 63.0 | 63.0 | 24.0 / -13.9 |
| 7 | E2–W2 | E2-W ↔ W2-E | 540 m | bridge: off-beam until engaged | 60.7 | 60.7 | 30.7 | 13.9 / -18.4 |
| 8 | E1–N | E1-N ↔ N-single | 504 m | bridge: off-beam until engaged | 63.0 | 63.0 | 34.1 | 15.0 / -13.9 |
| 9 | W1–S | W1-S ↔ S-single | 747 m | bridge: off-beam until engaged | 63.0 | 63.0 | 41.2 | 8.0 / -13.9 |

Chain per path: 20 dB pad on each sector port, a 2-way splitter where a port reaches two peers, 3 dB of jumpers (assumed), one programmable attenuator (0–63 dB). Down = attenuator at maximum: every path then sits at least 13.9 dB below the lowest MCS threshold (last column, clear-air margin in dB). Bridges capped at the maximum while waiting: E1–N, W1–S.

Before the event the attenuator's own insertion loss (up to ~17 dB at 0 dB for a 67 GHz solid-state unit) and the jumpers (~6 dB/m at 60 GHz for 1.85 mm cable) add to the chain: measure each path and subtract the excess from its setting. The lowest link-up setting (23.1 dB) leaves that much room. 1.85 mm parts are rated to 67 GHz, which covers Siklu's 57–66 GHz band (Terragraph channels 1–4).

These settings follow the MARL paper's radio model (about 145 dB of system gain at the lowest MCS). The N367 datasheet gives about 116 dB, so on the real radios calibrate each path in margin terms instead: find the attenuator value at which the link just drops, then back off by the margin in the last column (link up) and go at least 14 dB past it to take the link down.

Sector ports reaching two peers (2-way splitter each): E2-W, HUB-E, HUB-W, N-single, S-single, W2-E.

V-band parts: 9 programmable attenuators, 6 splitters, 12 pads (one per used sector port), 24 cables (two per path, one per splitter).

## Microwave hops

| Hop | Chain | At rest | At t0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1–CORE | transition → 30 dB pad → programmable attenuator → 30 dB pad → transition | 10 dB (+ fades) | maximum: taken down |
| CORE–E1 | transition → 30 dB pad → programmable attenuator → 30 dB pad → transition | 10 dB (+ fades) | maximum: taken down |
| W1–W2 | transition → 30 dB pad → programmable attenuator → 30 dB pad → transition | 10 dB (+ fades) | unchanged (can be taken down for other islands) |
| E1–E2 | transition → 30 dB pad → programmable attenuator → 30 dB pad → transition | 10 dB (+ fades) | unchanged (can be taken down for other islands) |

## Ethernet: site switches and what each port carries

**W1** (5 ports)

1. IP-50: microwave link W1–CORE
2. IP-50: microwave link W1–W2
3. TG DN: TG links E: HUB; S: S (bridge)
4. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
5. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

**W2** (4 ports)

1. IP-50: microwave link W2–W1
2. TG DN: TG links E: HUB, E2 (bridge)
3. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
4. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

**CORE** (5 ports)

1. IP-50: microwave link CORE–W1
2. IP-50: microwave link CORE–E1
3. TG DN: TG links N: N
4. TG controller: Terragraph controller (lost at t0)
5. DPIR server: DPIR planner (lost at t0)

**HUB**: no switch. The TG node's port only takes PoE power; it carries the hub links over the air interface and must not be wired to anything else.

**E1** (5 ports)

1. IP-50: microwave link E1–CORE
2. IP-50: microwave link E1–E2
3. TG DN: TG links N: N (bridge); W: HUB
4. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
5. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

**E2** (4 ports)

1. IP-50: microwave link E2–E1
2. TG DN: TG links W: HUB, W2 (bridge)
3. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
4. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

**S** (3 ports)

1. TG CN: TG links single: HUB, W1 (bridge)
2. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
3. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

**N** (3 ports)

1. TG CN: TG links single: CORE, E1 (bridge)
2. Agent PC: MARL agent + site routing
3. Traffic host: flow / service endpoint

Site switches: 7 (W1 5, W2 4, CORE 5, E1 5, E2 4, S 3, N 3 ports; 29 in all), plus one out-of-band management switch for the agent PCs' second NICs, the attenuator controllers, the PDUs and logging. One managed switch with a port-based VLAN per site also works, provided inter-VLAN routing stays off: the sites may only meet through the radio links.
